summary.title: How To Make A CPU - A Simple Picture Based Explanation
summary.one_liner: A high-level, step-by-step overview of how silicon wafers are grown, patterned with photolithography, etched, and packaged into CPU chips.
takeaways: The main CPU fabrication stages: grow a monocrystal silicon boule, slice it into wafers, pattern with photoresist and photomask, etch, repeat deposition and doping layers, then dice and package the die.
Die packaging connects the chip pads to package pins using bond wires or flip-chip solder balls.
Real fabrication is far more complex and proprietary; the article points to search terms like advanced optics for photolithography and lithographic metrology for further study.
Micron-scale hobbyist chip fabrication is described as feasible, while nanometer-scale features are not, and the author warns that real fab chemicals are hazardous.
summary.summary: The article walks through 19 numbered steps for making a CPU from rocks and sand, using plain-language pictures and short notes. It covers silicon purification, Czochralski crystal growth, wafer slicing and doping, photolithographic patterning with photoresist and a quartz mask, acid etching, repeated layer processes, dicing, and die packaging. The author stresses that real modern fabrication is far more complicated and proprietary, and lists search terms for deeper study. The page also includes a safety warning and mailing-list and related-article links, which are not summarized here.
